title: File system core in Java
idea: The core is a `FileSystem` facade: it parses each path into names, walks from the root to the target, and checks everything before changing the tree.

analogy.text: A postal sorter reads an address one line at a time: country, city, street, house. A missing line stops delivery with a clear reason.
analogy.breaks: Mail never moves a whole street to a new city.

points: `parse` turns a path into names and folds away `.` and `..` safely.
`resolve` walks names from the root and fails with a precise error code.
`move` checks everything before it detaches a node, so a refusal changes nothing.
`find` walks with an explicit stack; `size()` and `path()` still recurse.

steps.caption: `find` resolves the start path and pushes that one node on the stack.
Pop `ada/`. It is not a match. Push its children in reverse, so `docs/` ends on top.
Pop `docs/` and push its two files, again reversed to keep sorted order.
Pop `cv.pdf`. The test fails, and a file has no children to push.
Pop `notes.txt`. The test passes, so its full path joins the matches.
Pop `logs/` and push its one child, `app.log`.
Pop `todo.txt`. It matches. The stack is empty, so `find` returns both paths.

code.title: FileSystem facade
code.caption: Path parsing, resolution, mkdir -p, create, list, size, find, move and recursive delete, with one error type.

walk.text: Build a home folder, then list it, size it and find the text files.
Move and rename in one call, size through `..`, then delete a folder.
Five calls that must fail, each with its own error code.
Like `mkdir -p`: reuse folders that exist, create the rest.
`move` runs every check first; only then does it detach, rename and attach.
`parse` rejects relative paths and empty names, and stops `..` at the root.
`resolve` walks one name at a time; a file in the middle is an error.

pitfalls: Parse a path once into names, then walk; never re-split strings at each level.
Check that a folder is not moved into its own subtree, or it vanishes.
Detach a node only after every check passes, or a failed move loses data.

quiz.q: What does the fourth `error` line of FileSystem print?
quiz.why: The target's parent, `docs`, sits inside `/home`. Walking up from `docs` reaches `/home`, so `isInside` is true and the move is refused before anything changes.

takeaway: Parse once, resolve from the root, check everything, then mutate.

starters: How would I add a current working directory and relative paths?
Why is lexical handling of .. different from what a real OS does?
How do I make delete refuse non-empty folders unless asked to recurse?
